title: package install: OS_PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE for a package declaring a NEWER protocol major prescribes "migrate meta --from 19", which cannot apply
body:
Filing gate: ① a product defect with a live reproduction. The refusal prescribes a remedy that cannot apply, finding class (a), low.
Business reason: an operator who installs a package built for a NEWER protocol major than the runtime (`^19` on an 18 runtime) is told to run `objectstack migrate meta --from 19`. Migration only moves metadata forward from an older major. The real remedy is to upgrade the runtime, or to install a build of the package for this major, so the advice sends the operator into a dead end.
Reader: the protocol-handshake code (`declaredFloorMajor` / the `migrateCommand` detail in `protocol-handshake.ts`).
Dedupe (open AND closed): "OS_PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE migrateCommand newer major package ahead of runtime migrate meta --from" → 39 hits, none of them this one. The nearest are migrate-meta prescription cards (#22219, #17134), which are about older majors.
reach: public HTTP entry, measured at `756220c4` on a stock showcase boot (scratch copy), as admin.
Checklist item priority: P1
type: Bug
QA-source: #26476 · platform-core.manifest-install-contract · observed beside the clauses

Reproduction:
1. As admin, `POST /api/v1/packages` with `{"manifest":{"id":"com.example.qa-p-future","name":"x","version":"1.0.0","scope":"project","type":"app","engines":{"protocol":"^19"}}}`.
2. Actual: 422 `OS_PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE` with `details.migrateCommand` = `objectstack migrate meta --from 19`, and the message says "Run: objectstack migrate meta --from 19".
3. Control: `engines.protocol '^17'` → the same 422 with `--from 17`, which is correct.

**Expected:** when the declared floor major is above the runtime's protocol major, the refusal names the runtime upgrade (or a package build for this major) and carries no `migrateCommand`.

**Mechanism:** the declared floor major is turned into `--from N` without comparing its direction against `protocolVersion`.
